intended_object: Given a subfunctor S of G : D ⥤ Type w and a functor J : C ⥤ D, the restriction of S along J: the subfunctor of J ⋙ G with sections S(J X) at each X. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition is the usual restriction (whiskering) of a subfunctor along a functor. At each object X it takes the set S.obj (J.obj X), a subset of G.obj (J.obj X), which is by definition (J ⋙ G).obj X. Stability under a morphism f follows from S.map (J.map f), because (J ⋙ G).map f is definitionally G.map (J.map f). The categories, the functor J and the universes are all arbitrary, so the definition is fully general. Mathlib's `Subfunctor.preimage` pulls a subfunctor back along a natural transformation, not along a functor, and Mathlib has no subfunctor precomposition (I searched the `Subfunctor` directory and for subfunctors of composite functors `J ⋙ G`). So there is no Mathlib counterpart, and the definition is correct and at its natural generality.
